title: Completion of a quotient of a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring, $\lambda:A\to B$ a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with kernel $J$, and $\mathfrak n=\lambda(\mathfrak m)$, an ideal of $B$. Let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $A$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak n^n$ the $\mathfrak n$-adic completion of $B$, with canonical maps $c_A:A\to A^\wedge$ and $c_B:B\to B^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Since $\lambda(\mathfrak m^n)=\mathfrak n^n$, $\lambda$ induces surjections $A/\mathfrak m^n\to B/\mathfrak n^n$ and hence a ring map $\theta:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto(\lambda(x_n))_n$, with $\theta\circ c_A=c_B\circ\lambda$. Then $\theta$ is surjective and its kernel is $JA^\wedge$, the ideal of $A^\wedge$ generated by $c_A(J)$; hence $\theta$ induces a ring isomorphism $A^\wedge/JA^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}B^\wedge$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor, line 22901), parts (2) and (3), applied to the exact sequence of finite A-modules 0 -> J -> A -> B -> 0 and the ideal m (completion exact; B^ = B (x)_A A^ = A^/JA^), together with the observation that for the A-module B one has m^n B = n^n, so the m-adic completion of the A-module B is the n-adic completion of the ring B; used (with B = A/J) in the proof of More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PP via Algebra Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime).

proof.text: (The module completion of $B$ is the ring completion of $B$.) Regard $B$ as an $A$-module via $\lambda$ and $J$ as an $A$-submodule of $A$; let $P^\wedge=\varprojlim_nP/\mathfrak m^nP$ and $u^\wedge$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic module completions and completed maps of [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]. For every $n\ge1$, $\mathfrak m^nB$ (the $A$-submodule generated by the $a\cdot b=\lambda(a)b$, $a\in\mathfrak m^n$, $b\in B$) equals the ideal $\lambda(\mathfrak m^n)B$, and $\lambda(\mathfrak m^n)=\lambda(\mathfrak m)^n=\mathfrak n^n$ because $\lambda$ is a surjective ring map (the image of an ideal under a surjective ring map is an ideal, and the image of a product of ideals is the product of the images); as $\mathfrak n^n$ is an ideal, $\lambda(\mathfrak m^n)B=\mathfrak n^n$. So $B/\mathfrak m^nB=B/\mathfrak n^n$ for all $n$, with the same transition maps, and the $A$-module $\lim_nB/\mathfrak m^nB$ is, as a set with addition, the ring $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak n^n$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Likewise $A^\wedge$ (module completion of $A$ at $\mathfrak m$) is the ring $A^\wedge$. Under these identifications the completed map $\lambda^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto(\lambda(x_n))_n$, is exactly $\theta$; it is a ring map (componentwise) and $\theta\circ c_A=c_B\circ\lambda$ (both send $a$ to $(\lambda(a)\bmod\mathfrak n^n)_n$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local, line 44811), proof, where completeness of S = R/I 'as an R-module' (00MA) is used as completeness of the ring S; the identification m^n B = n^n of the m-adic module completion of B with the n-adic ring completion is implicit there and written out by the agent

proof.text: (Exactness.) $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so the ideal $J$ is a finitely generated $A$-module; $A$ is generated by $1$ and $B$ by $1=\lambda(1)$ as $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The sequence $0\to J\xrightarrow{\iota}A\xrightarrow{\lambda}B\to0$ ($\iota$ the inclusion) is an exact sequence of finitely generated $A$-modules ($\ker\lambda=J$, $\lambda$ surjective). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] with $I=\mathfrak m$, the sequence $0\to J^\wedge\xrightarrow{\iota^\wedge}A^\wedge\xrightarrow{\lambda^\wedge}B^\wedge\to0$ is exact. By Step 1, $\lambda^\wedge=\theta$; hence $\theta$ is surjective and $\ker\theta=\operatorname{im}\iota^\wedge$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor, line 22901), part (2), applied to 0 -> J -> A -> B -> 0 and the ideal m

proof.text: (The image of $J^\wedge$ is $JA^\wedge$.) Let $c_P:A^\wedge\otimes_AP\to P^\wedge$, $a\otimes x\mapsto a\cdot\iota_P(x)$, be the maps of [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (tensor product as in [def-weil-module-base-change]), for the ideal $\mathfrak m$ of the Noetherian ring $A$. Since $J$ is finitely generated (Step 2), $c_J$ is bijective by part (2), in particular surjective; by naturality, part (1), $\iota^\wedge\circ c_J=c_A\circ(\mathrm{id}_{A^\wedge}\otimes\iota)$. Hence $\operatorname{im}\iota^\wedge=\operatorname{im}(\iota^\wedge\circ c_J)=\operatorname{im}(c_A\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\iota))$. Every element of $A^\wedge\otimes_AJ$ is a finite sum $\sum_ky_k\otimes j_k$ ($y_k\in A^\wedge$, $j_k\in J$), and $c_A(\mathrm{id}\otimes\iota)(\sum_ky_k\otimes j_k)=\sum_ky_k\cdot\iota_A(j_k)=\sum_ky_kc_A(j_k)$, since $\iota_A=c_A:A\to A^\wedge$ and the $A^\wedge$-action on $A^\wedge$ is the ring multiplication (componentwise). The set of such sums is exactly the ideal $JA^\wedge$ of $A^\wedge$ generated by $c_A(J)$. With Step 2: $\ker\theta=JA^\wedge$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3) (M^ = M (x)_R R^), and Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), proof: 'J (x)_R R^ -> R (x)_R R^ = R^ ... is identified with J^ -> R^'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $\theta:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is a surjective ring homomorphism (Steps 1, 2) with kernel $JA^\wedge$ (Step 3), so by the homomorphism theorem for rings it induces a ring isomorphism $A^\wedge/JA^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}B^\wedge$, $x\bmod JA^\wedge\mapsto\theta(x)$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_local_completion_quotient (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) : let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A let n := m.map φ let Ahat := AdicCompletion m A let Bhat := AdicCompletion n B let cA := algebraMap A Ahat let cB := algebraMap B Bhat let Jhat := (RingHom.ker φ).map cA (∀ k : ℕ, (m ^ k).map φ = n ^ k) ∧ ∃ θ : Ahat →+* Bhat, (∀ k : ℕ, ∃ θk : (A ⧸ m ^ k) →+* (B ⧸ n ^ k), Function.Surjective θk ∧ θk.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (m ^ k)) = (Ideal.Quotient.mk (n ^ k)).comp φ ∧ (evalₐ n k).toRingHom.comp θ = θk.comp (evalₐ m k).toRingHom) ∧ θ.comp cA = cB.comp φ ∧ Function.Surjective θ ∧ RingHom.ker θ = Jhat ∧ ∃ e : (Ahat ⧸ Jhat) ≃+* Bhat, ∀ x : Ahat, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk Jhat x) = θ x
